summary: ACCEPT. D20 -- a confirmed Webull fill now consumes its venue-local resting/reclaim slot, closing the defect I measured on 08-27: ELEVEN filled buy orders across FIVE slots = SIX EXCESS FILLS (MIMI be9efe99 x2 and 4c32aec7 x2; PPCB dfcc2a77 x3, e59a2f0c x2, aa31a212 x2), spaced 4 to 56 minutes apart, each with a DISTINCT client_order_id -- so these were NEW ORDERS ON AN ALREADY-FILLED SLOT, not retries. All live:orb, slot=resting, qty 1, schwab_1m_v2- coids. THE LAYER IS CORRECT AND THIS MATTERED. The entry union was NEVER the missing control: it blocks only while an intent is non-terminal, median 0.105s, and these fills are minutes apart. Fixing it there would have re-created the cross-venue obstruction #843 had just removed. The fix is at slot consumption, which is where the #644 composition cap lives. ⭐ THE SCOPE CHOICE IS THE HEART OF THE REVIEW AND IT IS RIGHT: consumption is scoped to the SEGMENT, not the position -- the code comment states it survives a position close and claim expiry and resets only when the segment ends. That is exactly #644's documented cap (<=1 resting AND <=1 reclaim PER SEGMENT), so it is NOT one-entry-per-symbol-forever, which was the over-narrowing failure I went looking for. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Codex mutated only the guard; the OVER-NARROWING direction -- the one that silently COSTS ENTRIES -- was unmutated, so I ran it myself against an 8-test baseline in an isolated worktree with module provenance proven first. M-OVERNARROW, deleting the segment-end release `state.fanout_webull_resting_taken = False`: 2 FAILED -- test_segment_end_releases_both_webull_composition_slots and test_restart_replay_keeps_consumed_slot_through_historical_anchor_replay. M-GUARD, forcing _fanout_webull_slot_taken to return False: 6 failed / 2 passed, matching codex's report exactly. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 7564254950ed80d3. ⭐ THE REPLAY TEST DYING UNDER BOTH MUTANTS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: a restart replay must neither RE-OPEN a consumed slot nor KEEP a released one, and only a two-sided pair can show that. READING A IS PRESERVED AND EXPLICITLY TESTED: test_consumed_slot_blocks_the_schwab_fill_fanout_but_not_the_schwab_fill, and resting/reclaim remain independent per test_consumed_resting_slot_does_not_consume_webull_reclaim_slot. The Schwab primary and the opposite Webull slot stay independently eligible, which is the operator's standing decision and the thing a naive fix would have broken. ⛔ NOT MEASURED: I ran only the focused file for these two mutants, not the full suite -- codex reports 2,933 passed with 14 skipped, taken on report. I did not mutate the reclaim-side release (only resting), accepting it on the symmetry of lines 840-841. No live exercise exists: this is an entry-path change and its first real test is a live tape. ⛔⛔ DEPLOY: src/** => THIS REQUIRES A v2 RESTART. Do NOT deploy it before Monday's 06:00-06:45 restoration watch reports -- a restart resets the boot clock, and unlike the #843 case there IS now something to lose, because the box has been running the post-#843 configuration since 20:27Z Saturday and Monday's watch is the first and only observation of it. Deploy after the watch reports, or after Monday's close. PATCH IDENTITY: recomputed by me as cab566ed870cd2e4b330c36fc1e48eac7cfa881d.
